neighbours.label: Negative pole: English pre-emption phrases that stop a problem early: 'head off', 'nip (it in the bud)', and 'before it/they' right after a verb of stopping or treating a problem (not a plain time 'before')
fire: The manager stepped in to head off a dispute between the two teams.
We need to nip this rumor in the bud before Monday's meeting.
Treat the leak before it spreads into the drywall.
Regular checkups help doctors catch infections before they become serious.
The city tried to head off flooding by clearing the storm drains early.
A quick apology can nip a misunderstanding in the bud.
She fixed the bug before it could reach production.
Vaccines stop outbreaks before they start.
quiet: The manager stepped in after a dispute broke out between the two teams.
We need to discuss this rumor at Monday's meeting.
Wash the dishes before it gets dark outside.
Regular checkups are scheduled before they go on vacation.
The city cleaned up the streets after the flooding ended.
A quick apology can sometimes make a misunderstanding worse.
She ate lunch before it started to rain.
Vaccines are given to children at the local clinic.

predictions: 6/8 fire, at most 1 near miss; plain 'before' near misses should stay quiet
